issues_found: OWNER-VISIBLE: the build script is now `next build --webpack`. Serwist is a webpack plugin and Next 16 builds with Turbopack by default, which would silently produce no service worker. Dev stays on Turbopack with Serwist disabled, as g5 requires.

Two edits to eslint.config.mjs were made through a shell edit, each explicitly authorised by the owner after the config-protection hook blocked the normal edit: the architecture spread (3 lines) and the generated-worker ignore (3 lines). Neither weakens a rule.

A task 000 file, scripts/verify-architecture.mjs, was fixed: its JSONC parser read the '/*' in path aliases as a comment start and crashed on any real tsconfig. No invariant was changed; a regression test was added.

ESLint was downgraded from 10 to 9 (owner decision, raised as required by the task doc). Vitest is 4, not 5, because Vitest 5 needs a newer @types/node than the scaffold's ^20; revisit both when the scaffold's Node types are bumped.

Security: @serwist/next pins browserslist 4.28.6 with two high-severity advisories; an npm overrides entry pins 4.29.0. npm audit is 0 vulnerabilities. Remove the override once @serwist/next ships a fixed pin.
Two lint warnings remain and are not errors: an anonymous default export in eslint.architecture.mjs (task 000) and an unused Geist import in the create-next-app layout.tsx.
The story project uses the installed Chrome (channel chrome), so a machine without Chrome cannot run npm run test until Playwright's own browser is installed; there is no CI in the repo yet.

An earlier mistake was corrected: @serwist/turbopack was installed against the docs and then replaced by @serwist/next; and a PowerShell helper named Rd (an alias of Remove-Item) briefly deleted two tracked state files, restored from git with nothing lost.
